subsystems.name: Sorbent bed
subsystems.role: the working material: a porous solid that grabs water molecules from air and gives them up when warmed.
parts: metal-organic framework (MOF) crystals or hygroscopic salt

subsystems.name: Air handling
subsystems.role: moves ambient air past the sorbent so it can load up with moisture.

subsystems.name: Regeneration heat source
subsystems.role: drives the water back out of the sorbent.
parts: solar thermal collector or glazed panel

subsystems.name: Condenser and collector
subsystems.role: cools the released vapour back into liquid and gathers it.

subsystems.name: Water conditioning and storage
subsystems.role: makes the output safe to drink and holds it.

subsystems.name: Controls and power
subsystems.role: schedules the wet/dry cycles and runs the fans.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the sorbent
buildSteps.detail: Metal salts and organic linker molecules are reacted in solvent to grow MOF crystals with pores the right size to capture water. The solvent is then driven out to leave empty, open pores.

buildSteps.title: Stabilise and shape it
buildSteps.detail: Crystals are bound onto, or grown on, a porous support or coated onto metal fins, so air can reach the pores and heat can be pushed in and out quickly.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the adsorption module
buildSteps.detail: Sorbent-coated elements are stacked in trays inside a housing with an air inlet and outlet, sized so humid night air can pass through.

buildSteps.title: Build the regeneration side
buildSteps.detail: A glazed or evacuated-tube solar collector is coupled to the bed so daytime sun heats the sorbent and releases the captured vapour.

buildSteps.title: Add the condenser
buildSteps.detail: A cool surface, thermally linked to a shaded or sky-facing heat sink, condenses the released vapour; the water runs down into a tray.

buildSteps.title: Wire up controls and power
buildSteps.detail: Sensors track humidity and temperature; the controller opens the bed to air at night when relative humidity peaks and closes it to desorb in the day.

buildSteps.title: Deploy as an array
buildSteps.detail: Modules are mounted on ground frames or roofs and plumbed into a manifold feeding a shared storage tank.

buildSteps.title: Commission and verify
buildSteps.detail: Output per kilogram of sorbent is measured under local conditions, and the water is tested against drinking-water standards before use.

prerequisites.why: frameworks such as aluminium fumarate survive repeated cycling, but only a handful are proven for years of use.
the process is powered by sunlight, so its economics track solar costs.
frameworks are made at laboratory and pilot scale; tonne-scale production at low cost is the main barrier to farms.

prerequisites.tech: Efficient condensation in hot, dry air
prerequisites.why: below roughly 20–30% relative humidity there is little vapour to condense, so condenser design and sorbent affinity set the limit.
the adsorption/desorption rhythm must be tuned to local weather to get useful yields.

pathway.milestone: solar-driven MOF harvesters demonstrated in desert air, plus commercially sold rooftop units in dry regions
pathway.unlocks: drinking water where no well or pipe exists.

pathway.milestone: sorbent beds tuned for very low humidity and regenerated by waste heat rather than dedicated solar
pathway.unlocks: operation deeper into deserts and alongside industrial plants.

pathway.milestone: modular farms of thousands of square metres producing thousands of litres a day
pathway.unlocks: village and small-town supply, and irrigation for high-value crops.

pathway.milestone: large arrays on coastal deserts paired with solar farms
pathway.unlocks: a water source that does not depend on rainfall, rivers or aquifers.
